subject: history
title: After the Plague Adventure
welcome_lead: The plague is over — but England will never be the same. Fewer workers, angry peasants and the end of the old order. 🌾
meta_desc: After the Plague Adventure — a KS3 walkthrough of the social effects of the Black Death in England.
final_note: You saw how labour shortages, higher wages and the Peasants' Revolt all flowed from the Black Death.

concepts.def: Not enough workers for the work

walkthroughs.body_html:
By 1350 the first wave of plague had passed.

Historians think between 30% and 50% of people in England had died. Whole villages disappeared. Towns lost a third or more of their people.

It was the worst disaster in English history. 😔

With so few workers left, those still alive were suddenly valuable.

Peasants demanded higher wages and better conditions. They could leave their lord and find a new job somewhere else.

In 1351 Parliament passed the Statute of Labourers, trying to freeze wages at pre-plague levels and stop peasants moving. It did not really work.

The plague helped break the old feudal system:

  • Peasants had more freedom and money.
  • Many became free tenants, paying rent rather than working for a lord.
  • Anger at the Statute of Labourers and the 1381 poll tax led to the Peasants' Revolt.

Within a hundred years, the old serfdom was almost gone in England. The Black Death changed society forever. 🌱

mcqs.q: How was the Cuban Missile Crisis resolved?
options: Medieval people thought it was caused by germs they couldn't see.
Kennedy stared Khrushchev down and the Soviets backed off unconditionally.
A secret deal: the USSR withdrew missiles from Cuba; the US publicly pledged not to invade Cuba and secretly agreed to remove Jupiter missiles from Turkey.
The crisis ended when Castro persuaded Khrushchev to withdraw.

mcqs.q: How did the feudal system work in Norman England?
options: Feudalism was a written constitution introduced by William in 1066.
Medieval people thought it was caused by germs they couldn't see.
Feudalism meant peasants were slaves owned by the king.
The king granted land to tenants-in-chief in return for knight service; they in turn enfeoffed knights who held land in return for military service to their lord.
